Dance
Under review, not yet approved. New design: nothing here is in the app. Phone and desktop. Dance with a pass or fail from the community's owner is part of launch, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12, so everything on this sheet is launch work.
Getting here: a song's sheet has a Dance row beside Study and Karaoke, in Your songs (Screens/Songs/YourSongs) and in the rewards sheet opened from a post's pill (Parts/Rewards/SongEarnSheet). The row opens the song's dances.
Choosing an existing dance: a song has a page of its dances, a grid of videos, two across, that scrolls. The first tile is a plus, which starts a new dance. Tiles carry no handle, per the workspace_owner: people choose a dance for what it pays. A dance that pays has one pill in the feed's colours; one that pays nothing has none, and those come last. When a dance pays both a cash bonus and the lottery, the tile shows the cash bonus, which is the amount that tells dances apart; the lottery appears on the dance page. Two across, not three, because a pill does not fit on a three-across tile. A funder can attach a reward to any dance of a song or to one exact dance (Spec 021), so tiles can differ.
Tapping a dance opens it full screen and plays it, so the person watches a dance before deciding. This is its own page, not the Home feed: no bottom navigation and no action rail, only the video, who made it, all the dance's rewards, the arrow back to the grid, and one button, "Do this dance". A dance can only be chosen from here, after it has been watched. The next and previous dances are a swipe away. Tapping a pill would open the rewards sheet, as in the feed.
The camera is the same camera as a video post, with Upload at the bottom left.
Review is full screen and has one choice and one button. The choice is a switch, "Show publicly if it passes", on by default, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12, because public dances are what grows the site. Inside the same card, under the label, a second line says "Same rewards either way."; the workspace_owner asked for it to sit with the switch, not apart from it. The button is "Submit for review"; it sends the take and saves the choice. The switch stood on the Submitted page until that day, where a switch followed by Done read as if Done posted the take; the workspace_owner questioned it and it was moved here.
On desktop the same steps are cards in the main column, in order, above the phone screens: the dances grid (still two across), one dance with its rewards and "Do this dance", the camera, Review and Submitted. As on the video flow, the camera is the computer's webcam; that is my proposal.
The flow ends at Submitted, the page the dancer sees while the take is checked (Parts/Rewards/ActivityResult). It names the song and shows the rewards. It says nothing about whether the take will be public: the workspace_owner found that line unnecessary on 2026-10-12, the choice having just been made on Review. Done only closes the page.
Who checks, and for how long, per the workspace_owner on 2026-09-30: the owner of the dance's community checks the take privately, because there is no moderator role; the answer is pass or fail and is final; a take nobody checks within seven days of upload ends as not reviewed, which is not a fail. If it passes, the dancer qualifies for the reward either way, and the take is shown publicly only when the switch was on. If it does not pass, or is not reviewed, it is not shown, so a song only ever shows takes that really are its dance. That a private take earns the same is the intended rule, not built behaviour.
Automatic grading is deferred. A dance joins the lottery of the day it passes, and counts toward the streak for the day it was sent.
A new dance: the plus tile opens the same camera for that song. Its screens are not drawn again here; it ends in an ordinary public post (the Video sheet).
Learning the answer, two ways, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12, who kept the 2026-09-30 ruling and Notifications both. On the dance's own page a row above the button, "Your take", shows the state of the dancer's latest attempt at that dance: In review, Passed, Not passed or Not reviewed. Only that dancer sees it. It is drawn in the last group of this sheet. And a row in Notifications (Screens/Shell/Notifications) arrives when the answer does. Both open the same page (Parts/Rewards/ActivityResult): Submitted while in review, otherwise the result. The server keeps each take's status, visibility choice and rewards; neither route owns it. A passed, public take appears as a normal video post, in the feed and on the profile like any other.
Ruled on 2026-10-12: submission tracking does not go on the profile, and only real dance videos appear in a feed, as normal posts. The row shows the latest attempt only; no list or history of takes is drawn.
To reconcile before building, with the planned task records for the Spec 021 amendment and its implementation: the 2026-09-30 rulings let a dancer post without submitting and said passing does not control publication, where this sheet publishes only after a pass; they said there is no verdict screen, where the result page now exists by the 2026-10-12 ruling; they limit an owner-reviewed pass to rewards funded by that community or the song's owner, never platform-funded pools, where the result pages draw the daily lottery and a bonus; and a pass can satisfy a reward only for a dancer who has done their human verification, which no screen here asks for. The amendment must be ratified before implementation starts.
Not designed yet: whether Do this dance is offered while a take is in review; the Your take row on desktop; changing a take's visibility after sending; a dancer who is not a member of the dance's community; empty states.
Differs from the specs: Spec 021 describes automatic scoring, and the Spec 024 draft asks "just a video, my new dance, or a take" at Post. Both need amending.
Source: specs 021 and 024.
Desktop: the same steps as cards in the main column, in order. Under review, not yet approved.

Ruled by the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12, keeping the 2026-09-30 ruling: the dancer alone sees their latest attempt's state on the dance's page, and Notifications stays as well. One row at the foot of the page, only for a dancer who has sent a take of this dance, and only for the latest one. Four states: In review, Passed, Not passed, Not reviewed, each drawn in place. Tapping In review opens the Submitted page; tapping any of the other three opens that result. They are the same pages a notification opens (Parts/Rewards/ActivityResult). Nobody else sees the row.
Repeating a dance is a main use, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12: people try again to do better, and come back each day to be in that day's lottery. The long-term design is a check that comes back quickly, by AI; the owner's review is the first version of the same flow. At launch the wait is not short: the owner has up to seven days, so no screen may promise a quick answer or same-day eligibility. While a take is being checked the page has no Do this dance button (first screen); once it is answered the button is back under the row (the other three screens), and the result page offers Try again.
What a repeat earns: a second pass in the same drawing adds no second lottery entry; a pass that qualifies for a later drawing can earn that drawing's entry. This says nothing about the cash bonus, which is not assumed to repeat daily.
Rules that fight daily participation, for the coordinator to reconcile; none is settled here. Spec 021 section 5.1 allows one active session per account, dance and revision, so under owner review a waiting take blocks another attempt at the same dance and revision for up to seven days; several waiting takes of the same dance and revision cannot exist today. A dance joins the lottery of the day it passes. Moving that to the day it was sent is not a ready fix: Spec 015 freezes a drawing's participants before the ticket is bought, so a pass that arrives after the cutoff cannot join that closed drawing. The streak day (the day sent) and the lottery entry therefore need separate treatment.
Withdrawing a waiting take is in the 2026-09-30 draft as a state and has no screen; the reviewer recommends a Withdraw take action on the waiting Submitted page, with a confirmation.
Not drawn: withdrawal, and desktop. Not built.
